excludedMechanisms: Base and Spectrolite are independently owned repair strands
Effectful NL routines retain authorized service/child calls; no blanket value-only rewriting
Clear classifiers returning policy enums, IDs or evidence values remain unchanged
Runtime oracles, world goals/IDs/splits, return signatures and service grants do not change

validation.method: Exact comparison of changed files against their baseline git contents
validation.tests: No new prose-mirroring tests; deterministic coordinator code is unchanged. Model behavior is not claimed measured.

concreteExclusions.reason: resolveTurn selects a TurnDecision from supplied player state; reviewAdventureJourney.nl explicitly delegates writes to resolveTurn/changeTurn.nl, the only adventurePlayerTurn-scoped routine. decideReadiness composes combineFindings and returns observed reports. Neither planner demands a missing operation.

Calendar planner already explicitly returns source IDs/time bounds for its TS coordinator. Mail decision explicitly says the caller owns reads/handoff. Gmail continuation explicitly reports a recommendation, neither launching nor writing. Remaining selected Google routines classify typed observations or call their existing allowed read/helper functions.

Plan chooses readers/changes/checks as data; reviewUserNewsGoal.ts performs reconciliation and native reads. Other two selectors return an intent/null or policy result. No unavailable action demand found.

reviewSetup calls the existing readInventory.ts capability wrapper then a pure target selector. The caller dispatches the authorized pairing/development routines. No mutation is demanded from the selector. No SST edit, so c482 successor is not modified.

These are effectful routines with the named native mutation service grants. They apply the change and verify returned observations; their Step returns do not make them pure planners. Retained unchanged.

These already return explicit action/status policy values. Actual effects belong to existing caller subroutines; the delegation planner explicitly says the caller starts the normal runtime separately. No new contract wording needed.
